content.short: Rust is a low-level programming language used to write flexible smart contracts for Solana.
content.description: Rust, developed in 2010, is a versatile language designed to empower developers. It supports safe systems programming with strong memory management and built-in parallelism, enabling the creation of fast, reliable software without compromising safety. While widely used for Solana smart contracts, Rust is also employed across ecosystems such as Polkadot, Elrond, NEAR, and Zcash, demonstrating its flexibility for diverse blockchain and Web3 applications.

resources.title: Fearless Concurrency With Rust
resources.tldr: The post that explained why Rust's ownership rules eliminate data races at compile time rather than at runtime.

resources.title: Stability as a Deliverable
resources.tldr: Treats not breaking your users as a feature to be engineered rather than a promise to be made. The reasoning here shaped how Rust ships to this day.

resources.title: The Road to Rust 1.0
resources.tldr: What the team decided had to be true before calling a language finished enough to commit to. Useful reading for anyone versioning a protocol or an API.
